ISIC Grant Application

My Story.

A story about my journey from India to Finland, and now hopefully to Japan. About leaving comfort zones, finding a home far away from home, and trying to figure out what comes next in life.

India
Finland
Japan
02
The Beginning

Leaving India

I finished high school in India and spent a lot of that time being deeply interested in computer science, especially Data Science and Machine Learning. I applied to universities around the world and was fortunate to have been accepted by Aalto on a scholarship.

The programme looked amazing and everyone I spoke to talked about the student culture there with a lot of excitement.

So, I made the decision to leave home and move to Finland. At that time, I had no idea that this country would eventually become a second home to me.

03
Five Years Later

Finding a Home
in Finland

The last five years at Aalto University have honestly been some of the best years of my life.

I became deeply involved in Teekkari culture and spent a lot of my time volunteering in different AYY associations and committees. The most meaningful role for me was being a Fuksi Captain for the Data Science programme because I got the chance to help new students feel welcomed into the same community that welcomed me when I first arrived in Finland.

At the same time, I balanced full-time work alongside my studies and also took on two master's programmes (Business and Computer Science). Finland slowly stopped feeling like a foreign country and started feeling like home.

04
The Crossroads

Afraid to Leave My
Comfort Zone Again

Now that I am reaching the final stage of my studies, I realise I am facing a very familiar feeling again, which is the feeling of leaving behind my comfort zone.

Over the last five years: Teekkarikylä as a place, the people around me, the daily routines and the student community became a huge part of my life. The thought of leaving it behind after graduation feels scary.

That is one of the reasons why this exchange is important to me. I feel like it would help me transition into the next phase of my life instead of suddenly leaving behind everything that has now become familiar.

Picture I took. I enjoy photography and want to develop that a lot in Japan.

05
Why Japan

A Country I Always
Wanted to Experience

Japan has been my number one country to visit since I was a child.

Over the years I consumed a lot of Japanese media and picked up small parts of the language through it. I have loved cooking Japanese food and became very interested in the culture and way of life there. I have admired the calmness and respect that people in Japan have towards others and their surroundings.

What attracts me the most is not the country itself, but the feeling I associate with it. There is a sense of calmness and balance that I have always wanted to experience from being there. I plan to spend a lot of my time being with the nature in Japan and practicing photography.

I also look forward to meeting both local and exchange students there learning from different cultures and experiencing student life in a completely different environment to Finland.

日本
Japan
06
What I Seek

Time to Think About
What Comes Next

The last five years of my life has been very busy. I spent most of that time balancing studies, full-time work, volunteering and other responsibilities constantly moving from one thing to another.

I never really gave myself enough time to stop and think deeply about what I actually want after graduation. That is what I hope this exchange can give me. I want it to be a period where I can slow down a little, reflect on my future and figure out the direction I want to take after my graduation.

I am also taking a five-month break from work during this period because I want to spend some time building a few IT projects and ideas I have been passionate about for a long time. I do not know where they will lead yet, but I want to properly explore them.

07
The Hope

Coming Back
with Clarity

I hope this exchange helps me grow both personally and emotionally.

I want to leave my comfort zone, experience a new culture, spend time with people from around the world and return with a better understanding of myself and what I want from life moving forward.

Right now, I feel like I am standing between student life and the next stage of adulthood and this exchange feels like the right experience at the right time.

This would genuinely be an opportunity of a lifetime for me.

"And that's my story."
